Facade

fuh-SAHD -- from a root meaning 'face,' the outward appearance something presents. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Facade is an outward appearance, especially a false one that is maintained to conceal a less pleasant reality.

Behind its cheerful facade, the company was actually losing money every month.

Worked Example

A family posts only smiling vacation photos and celebratory announcements online, never once mentioning the financial stress and arguments happening at home.

That carefully maintained, misleading outward appearance is exactly what a facade is. Unlike 'appearance' alone, which can be perfectly honest, facade specifically implies the truth is being hidden.

How Strong Is It? — front → facade → veneer

front vs. facade

front vs. facade: Front is a very casual, everyday word for facade -- 'putting up a front' is common in relaxed speech, while facade sounds slightly more formal and often architectural in origin.

veneer vs. facade

veneer vs. facade: Veneer can feel thinner and more fragile than facade: a facade can be maintained for years, while a veneer often suggests just a very thin, easily cracked layer of politeness or civility.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — faci-/facc-

root — faci-/facc-: face (Italian/Latin (facciata, from facies))

Put it together

Put it together: Facade traces back to the Latin facies, meaning 'face' or 'appearance,' by way of Italian facciata. A facade, at its root, is literally the 'face' a building -- or a person -- presents to the world, which may or may not match what's inside.

Use the root in a new word: superficial

Use the root in a new word: superficial: His superficial charm made a great first impression, but coworkers soon noticed he never followed through on his promises.
